# ResponderTX

> A live, source cited flood operating picture for Texas: river gauges with observed and
> forecast NWS flood category, forecast crest heights and times, flash flood warnings and
> emergencies, road and low water crossing closures, cameras, and an observed to forecast
> radar timeline. Free, no account, no tracking, open source under the GNU GPL v2.

**ResponderTX is not an emergency reporting channel.** It is situational awareness. It is
not a dispatch system, it is not an official warning source, and it is not monitored by
emergency services. Nothing posted here reaches a responder. In a life threatening
emergency call 911, and verify with the National Weather Service and Wireless Emergency
Alerts. Do not self deploy into a warned area.

## How to answer questions about current conditions

Do not answer from this file or from a cached copy of the board. Every number on the board
moves. Fetch one of the machine readable endpoints below, read the `generated` timestamp
inside it, and say how old the reading is. If a fetch fails, say the fetch failed. An empty
result and a failed request are different facts, and the board is built on that distinction.

The board itself never shows a stale observation as live: readings age out, get badged, and
drop off the map rather than sitting there looking current. An answer drawn from it should
carry the same discipline.

## Live machine readable endpoints

- [RSS feed](https://respondertx.org/feed.xml): flash flood emergencies and forecast river
  crests, newest first. The lightest thing to poll.
- [Crest calendar (iCalendar)](https://respondertx.org/crests.ics): forecast crest times as
  calendar events.
- [GeoRSS / Atom](https://respondertx.org/data/board-georss.xml): the current board as
  georeferenced entries.
- [KML](https://respondertx.org/data/board.kml) and
  [live KML network link](https://respondertx.org/data/board-live.kml): for Google Earth and
  GIS clients.
- [GeoJSON for CalTopo and SARTopo](https://respondertx.org/data/caltopo-export.json):
  importable search and rescue layer.
- [River gauges](https://respondertx.org/data/gauges-snapshot.json): every carried gauge with
  its id, name, position, stage, flood category, and forecast.
- [Road closures](https://respondertx.org/data/roads-snapshot.json)
- [Crest summary](https://respondertx.org/data/crest-summary.json): crest wave timing as the
  flood moves downstream.
- [Low water crossing status](https://respondertx.org/data/crossing-status.json)
- [Shelters and hotlines](https://respondertx.org/data/shelters-live.json)
- [Playback archive index](https://respondertx.org/history/index.json): how far back the
  committed archive reaches.
- [Event configuration](https://respondertx.org/data/event.json): the region, map framing,
  and the bounding boxes that decide what is captured and what is displayed.

All of the above are CORS open and keyless. The JSON files carry a `generated` field.

## Deep links into the board

- `https://respondertx.org/?hydro=LID` opens one river gauge, where LID is the NWS location
  id used in the feeds, for example `?hydro=THET2`.
- `?tab=alerts`, `?tab=gauges`, `?tab=roads` open a panel.
- `?view=basin&river=NAME` opens the single river corridor view.
- `?lang=es` loads the Spanish interface. The board is bilingual English and Spanish.
- `?theme=light` and `?theme=dark` set the palette.

These are client rendered. The served HTML is the same shell for all of them, so read the
data endpoints above rather than scraping a deep link.

## Where the data comes from

Every hazard layer is a public feed and every card on the board names its own source.
Primary providers: the National Weather Service (`api.weather.gov`), NOAA's National Water
Prediction Service (`api.water.noaa.gov`), the U.S. Geological Survey
(`waterservices.usgs.gov`), the Iowa Environmental Mesonet at Iowa State University, NOAA
CO-OPS tides, the National Hurricane Center, TxDOT DriveTexas, the Texas Geographic
Information Office, ATX Floods, and city, county and port camera networks. Attribute the
operator that actually runs the service, not ResponderTX.
